summary: WebDAV (RFC 4918) is an HTTP extension that turns a web server into a read/write filesystem via extra verbs (PROPFIND, PROPPATCH, MKCOL, COPY, MOVE, LOCK, UNLOCK) and PUT/DELETE. To an attacker an internet-facing WebDAV mount is a filesystem: it enumerates paths a normal spider can't reach (PROPFIND Depth:1/infinity), and where write verbs are unauthenticated it collapses straight to arbitrary file write and — on a server that also executes uploaded scripts (IIS ASP/ASPX, PHP handlers, JSP) — pre-auth RCE. Recce today only sends a single Depth:1 PROPFIND against seven hard-coded paths and reports a single 'WebDAV enabled' finding; it never enumerates the full verb allow-list from OPTIONS, never abuses Depth:infinity, never chains PUT+GET+execution, never tries MKCOL/COPY/MOVE, and never fingerprints the backend (mod_dav_fs vs mod_dav_svn vs SabreDAV vs IIS WebDAV vs nginx dav_ext). Promoting webdav_probe to services/webdav.py lets us treat WebDAV as a first-class service with its own tab, its own findings, and a per-mount attack path — a genuine exploit chain rather than a one-line 'enabled' info leak.

existing_coverage.notes: WebDAV rides on HTTP, so svcdetect/serviceenum recognise it via the underlying HTTP port — no separate detector needed. Real coverage today: (a) webdav_probe() at recce/services/http.py:1277 fires a single Depth:1 PROPFIND against ['/','/webdav/','/dav/','/share/','/public/','/files/','/uploads/'] and reports 207/multistatus as a medium 'http-webdav' finding; (b) recce/services/web/__init__.py:184-213 enumerates OPTIONS Allow and, when PUT is listed and active, runs _prove_put (checks.py:399) — a PUT->GET->DELETE roundtrip that emits 'Arbitrary file write via HTTP PUT (proven)'. Nothing else: no PROPFIND Depth:infinity, no MKCOL/COPY/MOVE/LOCK enum, no XXE via the PROPFIND request body (Content-Type: application/xml is sent but empty), no PUT->execute chain (only PUT->read), no anonymous vs authenticated differential, no Sabre/IIS/mod_dav banner fingerprint, no upload-through-COPY (IIS 6.0 CVE-2017-7269 double-extension trick), no lock-null-resource enum. The 'http-webdav-scan' constant in parser.py/scanner.py is an nmap NSE script id, not a native probe.

capabilities.name: options_dav_header_enum
capabilities.description: Parse OPTIONS response DAV: header (values 1/2/3) plus Allow: to fingerprint the WebDAV compliance class and the full server-declared verb set before touching state.
capabilities.notes: DAV: 1 = base, 2 = locking, 3 = revisions/versioning (RFC 3253). No verb tried yet — pure header read, folds MS-Author-Via and Public: too.

capabilities.name: propfind_depth_infinity_enum
capabilities.description: PROPFIND with Depth: infinity against each accepting mount to recursively enumerate the entire tree in one request — reveals directory layout normal spiders never see.
capabilities.notes: A server that honours Depth:infinity is BOTH an information disclosure AND a self-inflicted DoS surface (§9.1.4 explicitly warns). Cap the parsed response at ~2 MiB so a huge tree doesn't wedge the scan.

capabilities.name: verb_allowlist_enum
capabilities.description: Send each RFC 4918 verb (PROPFIND, PROPPATCH, MKCOL, COPY, MOVE, LOCK, UNLOCK) with a benign body against a discovered mount and record which return 2xx/207/401 vs 405 — the real allow list, not just OPTIONS.
capabilities.notes: Servers routinely lie in OPTIONS: mod_dav advertises MKCOL/COPY/MOVE even when Limit blocks them. Empirical enum is the truth. Use a temporary /recce_dav_probe_<rand>/ collection created via MKCOL and torn down via DELETE — never touch existing paths.

capabilities.name: anonymous_put_probe
capabilities.description: Attempt unauthenticated PUT of a small text marker to each writable-looking mount, GET it back to confirm write->read roundtrip, then DELETE — proves anonymous arbitrary file write.
capabilities.notes: Extend the existing _prove_put helper: run WITHOUT Authorization first, then WITH creds if provided, so anonymous vs credentialed writes surface as separate findings. Cleanup via DELETE (§9.6) or MOVE to /trash-<rand>/.

capabilities.name: put_webshell_chain
capabilities.description: When anonymous PUT is confirmed AND the server signature or file-extension mapping indicates a script handler (PHP/ASP/ASPX/JSP), PUT a language-appropriate one-liner and issue a single benign command (echo <computed nonce>) to prove RCE — cleanup via DELETE.
capabilities.notes: Gate on the same --exploit / upload_shell flag the web package already uses (recce/services/web/__init__.py:127). Nonce must be a computed value (e.g. shell arithmetic) so plain reflection can't false-positive. Try the classic IIS 6.0 `.asp;.txt`/`;.jpg` bypass and `.aspx` where server=Microsoft-IIS/6.0.

capabilities.name: mkcol_writable_collection
capabilities.description: MKCOL /recce_dav_probe_<rand>/ against each candidate root — a 201 Created proves the tester can create arbitrary directories, a write primitive and a prerequisite for COPY-based staging.
capabilities.notes: Followed by DELETE for cleanup. Distinguish 201 (created) from 405/409 (parent missing) to avoid noise.

capabilities.name: copy_move_upload_bypass
capabilities.description: Upload a benign resource with an inert extension via PUT (e.g. .txt), then COPY/MOVE it to a script extension (.asp/.php/.jsp) inside a writable collection — proves the classic IIS 6.0 CVE-2017-7269 / mod_dav upload-filter bypass.
capabilities.notes: Cleanup: DELETE both source and destination. Only fire when server-signature or DAV: header indicates IIS or Apache mod_dav, to keep FP rate low.

capabilities.name: propfind_xxe_probe
capabilities.description: Send a PROPFIND with an XML body that references an external entity (file:///etc/hostname or an internal callback URL) — a legacy Sabre/DAV or Xerces-based parser that resolves it echoes the content back inside the multistatus response.
capabilities.notes: The existing webdav_probe sends an EMPTY XML body — trivially extend it. Reuse recce/services/web/checks.py _XXE_LINUX/_XXE_HIT helpers so the file-read proof is consistent with other XXE findings. Only fire the external-DNS variant when an OOB callback host is configured (env var), never invent a random one.

capabilities.name: auth_scheme_and_realm_enum
capabilities.description: Read WWW-Authenticate on a 401 PROPFIND to record realm, offered schemes (Basic/Digest/NTLM/Negotiate), and Digest algorithm/qop/nonce reuse; Basic-over-cleartext on WebDAV feeds the credential-quickconnect path.
capabilities.notes: Realm string often names the mount (e.g. 'SVN Repository') — that name is a domain/host hint worth wiring to known_hostnames.

capabilities.name: backend_fingerprint
capabilities.description: Fingerprint the WebDAV implementation (Apache mod_dav_fs / mod_dav_svn, IIS WebDAV, nginx dav_ext, SabreDAV, Nephele, Nextcloud/ownCloud) via Server:, X-Dav-Powered-By:, MS-Author-Via:, and response-body namespaces — steers subsequent CVE mapping.
capabilities.notes: The identified product/version should be pushed back onto Port.product so it flows into the existing offline CVE DB pivot.

capabilities.name: lock_null_resource_enum
capabilities.description: LOCK against a non-existent path to detect lock-null-resource behaviour and to prove locking is unauthenticated — an attacker can create a lock-null resource that persists and blocks legitimate PUT/MKCOL.
capabilities.notes: Extract the Lock-Token from the response and immediately UNLOCK to leave no state behind.

capabilities.name: svn_repo_probe
capabilities.description: When mod_dav_svn is fingerprinted, request /!svn/vcc/default and /.svn/entries for the repository root revision and the anonymous-checkout allow bit — full source-tree leak if either responds 200.
capabilities.notes: Overlaps with the gitdump module — call a gitdump-style enumerator when a repo root responds, so recovered author emails feed known_users.

capabilities.name: if_header_auth_bypass
capabilities.description: Some legacy IIS/mod_dav stacks skip URL canonicalisation when an `If:` header supplies a resource token — retry a 401 PROPFIND with a bogus If: to test the CVE-2017-7269-adjacent bypass class.
capabilities.notes: Low-noise: one extra request per 401 mount. Only escalate to a write attempt when the bypass returns 207 where the plain request returned 401.

capabilities.name: cross_mount_pivot
capabilities.description: After PROPFIND enumeration, feed every discovered href back through the HTTP path-enum queue and the recce config-backup detector — .git/, backup/, .env, wp-config.php often sit inside DAV mounts invisible to a plain crawl.
capabilities.notes: Pure re-use of recce/services/http.py:path_enum classifier; no new network cost beyond the PROPFIND that already ran.

recommended_findings.title: WebDAV directory tree disclosed via PROPFIND Depth:infinity
Anonymous WebDAV PUT — arbitrary file write (proven)
WebDAV MKCOL — writable collection creation allowed
WebDAV Basic auth over cleartext channel
WebDAV LOCK accepts unauthenticated lock-null resources
WebDAV hrefs disclose sensitive paths (.git, backup, wp-config)

cross_service_wire_candidates: known_hostnames: WWW-Authenticate realm strings frequently name the mount ('SVN Repository', 'intranet-fs') and href responses leak internal hostnames in absolute Location: headers
known_users: mod_dav_svn PROPFIND responses embed <D:creator-displayname> for every file — SVN authors become usernames; Nextcloud/ownCloud DAV surfaces expose owner UIDs the same way
known_hashes: an in-tree /passwd, /.htpasswd, or /web.config recovered via PROPFIND+GET yields Basic/Digest/NTLM hashes — route into the shared hash surface so hashcat picks them up
known_domains: SVN commit-author emails and Nextcloud user emails found via PROPFIND properties

relay_targets: a confirmed anonymous-write WebDAV mount is a payload staging host for other services (SMB->WebDAV mapping, download-then-execute) — should be published as a relay/staging target the exploit-session-wiring layer can consume
NEW surface — known_uploaded_shells: when webdav_put_rce fires, record the URL of every uploaded shell so the P5 persistence-cleanup sweep can DELETE it if the run is aborted before local cleanup

recommended_hashcat_modes.description: NTLM — recovered from web.config <credentials> or IIS WebDAV backends
Apache $apr1$ MD5 — .htpasswd files that PROPFIND+GET recovers from a mod_dav_fs mount
descrypt — legacy /etc/passwd style, when PROPFIND on a misconfigured / mount exposes a passwd file
md5crypt — same route, modern Apache htpasswd -m
NetNTLMv1 — captured from a Negotiate/NTLM WebDAV challenge if the module logs the full exchange

implementation_notes: Refactor path: create recce/services/webdav.py containing a WebdavProbe class, move webdav_probe + _prove_put logic there, and reduce recce/services/http.py:webdav_probe + recce/services/web/__init__.py PUT-proof block to thin shims that import and delegate — matches the pattern already used for db/ wrappers (commit 27e29e3). Style-match recce/services/ftp.py: a module docstring naming the two layers (unauth passive vs credentialed/anonymous active), a _KNOWN_BAD table for CVE-mapped backend signatures (SabreDAV <1.7.11 XXE, IIS 6.0 CVE-2017-7269, mod_dav_svn CVE-2013-1849), and a single build_findings(host_ip, port, active, upload_shell) entry point returning list[Vuln] via svccommon.finding_builder. Reuse recce/services/web/checks.py _fetch/_prove_put — do not re-implement urllib boilerplate. Every state-changing verb MUST use a randomised path prefix (recce_dav_probe_<8-hex>) and guarantee cleanup in a try/finally so an interrupt never leaves droppings — feeds the P5 persistence-cleanup sweep. Depth:infinity responses must be size-capped (2 MiB) to prevent scan wedging. XXE and RCE probes MUST gate on the existing --exploit / active flag; nothing else should escalate past --active. No new dependencies — stdlib urllib + xml.etree.ElementTree (defusedxml if already in the tree). Keep 'http-webdav' as an alias script_id so historical scan diffs don't break; new findings adopt 'webdav-*' ids and get their own tab in the docx/xlsx reports.
